course_goals.text: Analyze the foundational concepts, historical evolution, and human sensory factors governing Extended Reality systems.
Understand the technical architecture of XR systems, including hardware components, tracking mechanisms, and software development principles.
Apply systematic design and implementation methodologies to develop, evaluate, and refine interactive XR systems.
Explain and apply advanced techniques for managing computational resources, optimizing rendering, and solving complex navigation problems in immersive environments.
Implement and develop basic Extended Reality applications using industry-standard platforms.

L01.lecture_goal: Introduce the foundational concepts, definitions, and practical importance of Extended Reality (XR) technologies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the core concepts of XR and distinguish between common public perceptions and technical applications.
You'll be able to define Extended Reality (XR) and explain the components of the reality-virtuality continuum.
You'll be able to justify the growing commercial importance of XR and outline the scope and structure of the course.

L02.lecture_goal: Analyze the application domains and system categories of extended reality technologies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and describe the application domains and market potential of extended reality technologies.
You'll be able to differentiate between non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive VR systems.

L03.lecture_goal: Analyze the diverse application domains and system categories of Augmented and Virtual Reality.

objectives.text: You'll be able to differentiate between the various application domains and technical types of Augmented Reality systems.
You'll be able to compare and contrast the system categories and application focuses of Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality.

L04.lecture_goal: Understand the defining characteristics and classification methods of Virtual Reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and explain the three defining characteristics of a Virtual Reality system.
You'll be able to apply the three characteristics to classify different systems.

L05.lecture_goal: Define and distinguish the core concepts of Augmented, Virtual, and Mixed Reality.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the core characteristics of Augmented Reality and compare it to Virtual Reality systems.
You'll be able to identify the course's working assumptions regarding Mixed Reality and summarize the key differences between VR, AR, and MR.

L06.lecture_goal: trace the historical evolution of Virtual and Augmented Reality from its foundational concepts to its current market growth.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and describe the distinct historical phases and key foundational inventions of Virtual and Augmented Reality.
You'll be able to trace the historical evolution of VR technologies and concepts across the mid-century (1950–1990) and modern phases (1990–2015).
You'll be able to understand the key milestones and drivers propelling the current growth of VR.

L07.lecture_goal: trace the historical evolution of Augmented Reality from its foundational concepts to its modern commercial applications.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how augmented reality and virtual reality systems developed from foundational research through early historical examples and defined phases.
You'll be able to describe the evolution of AR tools and applications from the mid-1990s onward, detailing key commercial milestones and drivers.

L08.lecture_goal: Analyze the foundational concepts, challenges, and experiential qualities of virtual and augmented reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to summarize the foundational concepts and identify the major technological and psychological issues in VR and AR systems.
You'll be able to explain the concepts of immersion and presence, including their components and the relationship between them in VR systems.

L09.lecture_goal: Examine the technical issues and fundamental concepts governing the development of Virtual and Augmented Reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to analyze the challenges of achieving presence in VR using fidelity concepts and explain the requirements and pose determination phases of Augmented Reality systems.
You'll be able to identify the major issues and concepts in VR and AR systems.

L10.lecture_goal: Analyze the causes and symptoms of cybersickness.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define cybersickness and explain the internal factors that contribute to its occurrence.
You'll be able to explain various hardware factors that induce cybersickness.

L11.lecture_goal: understand the factors that contribute to cybersickness and the various methods used to measure its severity.

objectives.text: You'll be able to analyze how specific VR content factors influence the severity of cybersickness.
You'll be able to identify the categories of input and compare manual and automated techniques used to measure cybersickness.

L12.lecture_goal: Master the principles of cybersickness, from its evaluation and modeling to the application of effective mitigation strategies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the evaluation framework for cybersickness, comparing various ML models and differentiating between detection and prediction methods.
You'll be able to analyze the challenges of cybersickness mitigation and apply various techniques, including FOV adjustments, optical flow manipulation, and hardware countermeasures.
You'll be able to summarize the causes, measurement, and comprehensive mitigation strategies for cybersickness.

L13.lecture_goal: Analyze the structure, components, and input mechanisms that constitute a complete VR hardware system.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain and define the holistic components and data flow of a complete VR system.
You'll be able to define and categorize the three essential components of VR hardware systems.
You'll be able to compare and contrast various VR input devices and analyze the functionality and limitations of non-hand-based tracking technologies.

L14.lecture_goal: Analyze the core components and peripheral devices that constitute a functional VR system.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the mechanisms of non-hand input devices and understand the role and components of the processing element in VR systems.
You'll be able to classify and describe the various output devices, including visual displays, haptic rendering systems, and motion platforms.

L15.lecture_goal: analyze the structure, function, and diverse implementations of augmented reality hardware systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and compare the components and features of various AR devices, including headsets and smart glasses.
You'll be able to classify AR devices based on their operational mechanisms and characterize the principles of Spatial AR systems.
You'll be able to describe various hardware implementations and compare different AR display technologies, from HUDs to contact lenses.
You'll be able to summarize the five categories of AR hardware systems covered in the lecture.

L16.lecture_goal: understand the principles and processes of tracking technology.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare the requirements and methods of tracking across different environments and sensor configurations.
You'll be able to explain the fundamental steps and outline the components of the tracking process.

L17.lecture_goal: Understand the principles and mechanisms required to accurately track movement using sensor data.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the types of trackers and the four stages of the tracking process.
You'll be able to define the Inertial Measurement Unit and explain the role of its components in tracking.
You'll be able to explain how sensor data is processed, including calibration, dynamic orientation calculation, and drift correction.
You'll be able to describe the complete process of sensor tracking, integrating calibration, registration, and drift correction.

L18.lecture_goal: understand the diverse principles, mechanisms, and applications of modern tracking technologies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the structure and types of electromechanical tracking devices and compare the mechanisms of electromagnetic and acoustic tracking systems.
You'll be able to identify and explain the mechanisms of vision-based, infrared, and visible light tracking systems, including 3D structure tracking.
You'll be able to compare inertial and GPS sensors and describe the components and types of tracking used in motion capture systems.
You'll be able to define hybrid tracking and summarize the lecture's scope and future topics.

L19.lecture_goal: understand the principles, processes, and challenges involved in developing effective VR and AR experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the foundational role of software in VR/AR and contrast ideal versus practical application development approaches.
You'll be able to describe the function of the Virtual World Generator (VWG) and explain the methods required for creating a virtual world.
You'll be able to analyze the technical challenges of maintaining motion correspondence and evaluate how user locomotion impacts cyber sickness and software design.

L20.lecture_goal: Analyze the fundamental concepts, components, and development methodologies required for building modern VR software.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the key components and understand the necessity of physics support within virtual world generators.
You'll be able to describe the components and interaction requirements of networked collaborative VR systems.
You'll be able to compare primary VR development approaches and understand the structure and function of VR game engines.
You'll be able to distinguish between native and web deployment methods and review key concepts in VR software development.

L21.lecture_goal: Analyze the structure, components, and development methods of AR software.

objectives.text: You'll be able to categorize AR software tools based on required programming skill and explain how low-level libraries and scene graphs form comprehensive AR frameworks.
You'll be able to understand how rapid prototyping tools simplify the development of AR experiences.

L22.lecture_goal: Analyze the diverse tools and methodologies available for developing augmented reality software.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare various AR development approaches and evaluate the benefits and limitations of plugin-based tools.
You'll be able to understand the characteristics and utility of standalone AR authoring tools.
You'll be able to summarize the core concepts of AR software and anticipate future topics.

L23.lecture_goal: Understand how human factors and user-centric design principles are essential for creating effective and invisible interactive systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how the concept of 'disappearing technology' relates to the evolution of computing toward invisible, interactive systems.
You'll be able to contrast the negative impact of technical jargon with the principles of a user-centric design approach.
You'll be able to analyze the necessity of incorporating human factors into system design by defining HCI and comparing different user types.

L24.lecture_goal: analyze the principles of design, usability, and human factors necessary for developing interactive XR systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to apply the three-class user categorization and compare various design perspectives to inform the development lifecycle of interactive systems.
You'll be able to define usability criteria and metrics, and explain the principles of user-centered design.
You'll be able to describe the architecture and human factors required for interactive XR systems.

L25.lecture_goal: Analyze the relationship between human sensory biology and the design principles required for effective extended reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how perceptual psychology informs the design of effective XR systems and how the human perceptual system interacts with virtual reality.
You'll be able to identify the components, organs, and receptors that constitute various human sensory systems.

L26.lecture_goal: Analyze the relationship between human sensory processing and the design challenges inherent in immersive XR systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how perception is biologically and computationally achieved by integrating neural network analogies, hierarchical processing, and long-term knowledge.
You'll be able to define proprioception and explain the brain's mechanism for processing body position and movement.
You'll be able to explain the mechanism of sensory mismatch and its resulting effects within immersive XR systems.
You'll be able to summarize the lecture's scope and outline future topics relevant to XR design.

L27.lecture_goal: understand the fundamental principles of light propagation and the physiological processes that enable visual perception.

objectives.text: You'll be able to justify the study of visual perception and light propagation, and compare the various physical descriptions of light and how it interacts with surfaces.
You'll be able to trace the path of light through the eye, explain the mechanisms of color perception, and compare the functions of different visual components and types of vision.

L28.lecture_goal: analyze the principles of human visual perception and apply this knowledge to the design and optimization of immersive reality (XR) systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the anatomical components and optical mechanisms of the human eye, including how it focuses light onto the retina.
You'll be able to explain how optical devices, such as VR headsets, function and how the human brain achieves depth perception using various visual cues.
You'll be able to compare the technical requirements for immersive systems, defining degrees of freedom and identifying key perceptual and resolution factors influencing hardware design.
You'll be able to summarize the key concepts of visual perception and their practical application in the design of extended reality (XR) systems.

L29.lecture_goal: Analyze the fundamental physics and biological mechanisms of sound to understand its critical role in creating immersive extended reality experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the role of auditory senses and how auditory input enhances immersion and presence in VR systems.
You'll be able to define sound, explain its propagation mechanism and wave properties, and describe the mechanism of hearing.

L30.lecture_goal: Analyze the principles of auditory perception and their application in creating immersive XR experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and describe the three levels of sound perception and define psychophysics, psychoacoustics, and the laws governing perceived sound.
You'll be able to apply psychophysical laws to predict auditory perception in VR systems.

You'll be able to explain the principles of pitch perception and sound localization, define the parameters and cues used for auditory localization, and explain the role of HRTF in synthesizing and and.
You'll be able to summarize the key concepts of sound and its role in immersive XR experiences.

L31.lecture_goal: explore how integrating non-visual human senses enhances the immersion of XR systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the remaining senses and their relevance to building immersive XR systems.
You'll be able to describe the somatosensory system and the six types of haptic exploration, and explain the role of haptic perception and its various implementation methods in XR systems.
You'll be able to analyze the principles and current state of smell and taste interfaces in XR systems.
You'll be able to summarize the discussion on human senses and preview interactive system development.

L32.lecture_goal: master the stages and principles of the Interactive System Development Lifecycle.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define the principles of user-centric design and explain its role in creating usable and acceptable interactive systems.
You'll be able to explain the necessity of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) and describe how iterative processes are used to analyze design challenges.
You'll be able to describe the stages of interactive system development, compare different evaluation methods, and explain the principles of managing iterative loops.

L33.lecture_goal: Introduce the challenges and technological solutions involved in preserving Majuli's cultural heritage using immersive technologies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to understand how the Majuli case study serves as a framework for XR system development.
You'll be able to analyze the geographical, cultural, and ecological significance of Majuli and the threat of erosion it faces.
You'll be able to define digital heritage preservation and outline the objectives and scope of the Majuli VR project.

L34.lecture_goal: understand the process of developing a cultural heritage VR system from initial challenges to final implementation.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the core challenges for developing the Majuli Island VR system.
You'll be able to analyze the methodology and data used to create the Majuli cultural heritage archive.
You'll be able to identify the key technical and design challenges in creating the Majuli VR tour.

L35.lecture_goal: master the process of gathering and specifying usability requirements for system design.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare system-centered and user-centered design approaches, and distinguish between end-user requirements and technical implementation details.
You'll be able to compare and define functional and non-functional requirements in system design.
You'll be able to define usability and outline the initial steps for gathering end-user requirements.
You'll be able to explain the Contextual Inquiry method and its role in gathering usability requirements.
You'll be able to demonstrate how contextual inquiry ensures usable system design through a case study.

L36.lecture_goal: Master the process of gathering, analyzing, and specifying usability requirements using contextual inquiry and affinity diagram techniques.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the modes and principles of conducting contextual inquiry and outline its stages and key requirements.
You'll be able to apply the affinity diagram method to analyze collected usability data and identify usability requirements.
You'll be able to apply sorting and header creation to categorize usability requirements and organize observational notes using affinity diagrams.
You'll be able to distinguish between usability requirements and implementation prescriptions, and apply the full process to specify and refine requirements using hierarchical grouping.

L37.lecture_goal: master the process of gathering, defining, and structuring usability requirements for complex systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to apply contextual inquiry outcomes and user research methods to define and structure functional requirements for a system.
You'll be able to analyze major usability challenges in VR systems and explain how specific research methods address them.
You'll be able to summarize the requirement gathering process and transition to the design phase.

L38.lecture_goal: design effective and usable interactive systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to outline the stages of the interactive system development lifecycle and understand the starting points and methods for interface and interaction design.
You'll be able to distinguish between various design guidelines, differentiate between specific and generic guidelines, and apply the principle of universal usability.
You'll be able to apply design principles for providing informative feedback, achieving task closure, preventing errors, and limiting short-term memory load in interface design.
You'll be able to identify and categorize the core interaction techniques used in immersive extended reality systems.

L39.lecture_goal: Analyze the core principles and techniques governing object interaction, selection, and manipulation in immersive virtual environments.

objectives.text: You'll be able to classify the main types of interaction and compare various hand selection techniques used in virtual and augmented reality.
You'll be able to compare basic ray casting with advanced selection techniques, including bend cast, depth ray, image plane, and volumetric methods.
You'll be able to describe the various techniques used for manipulating virtual objects in immersive environments.

L40.lecture_goal: Master the principles of locomotion, wayfinding, and system control necessary to design effective immersive virtual environments.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define navigation and classify the types and techniques of locomotion used in immersive settings, comparing walking-based methods and describing the main categories of VR locomotion.

You'll be able to explain how wayfinding builds a cognitive map using specific types of spatial knowledge and identify various methods for providing effective wayfinding support in complex virtual and.
You'll be able to identify various interaction techniques for system control and review core course concepts.

L41.lecture_goal: understand the comprehensive design process for creating a high-quality, immersive virtual reality tour system.

objectives.text: You'll be able to apply theoretical design knowledge to define the scope and user requirements for a virtual tour system.
You'll be able to describe the design elements and content processing techniques used to establish the virtual tour's starting experience and realism.
You'll be able to explain the system's interactive features, navigation mechanisms, and multimedia delivery methods.
You'll be able to summarize design techniques for minimizing cyber-sickness and review the lecture scope.

L42.lecture_goal: understand the principles, cycles, and techniques required for effective XR system implementation.

objectives.text: You'll be able to summarize the scope of XR system implementation and its foundational concepts.
You'll be able to explain the necessity of iterative development cycles and differentiate between horizontal and vertical prototyping approaches.
You'll be able to apply various prototyping techniques, including low-fidelity design, storyboarding, and the Wizard of Oz method, to visualize complex user interactions.

L43.lecture_goal: Master the techniques for prototyping and evaluating system designs.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare and contrast the three main methods for using prototypes in system development.
You'll be able to describe and apply various prototype evaluation procedures, including quick expert evaluation, cognitive walkthrough, and heuristic evaluation.

L44.lecture_goal: analyze the complete process of designing, evaluating, and implementing XR systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare and explain user evaluation techniques and identify specialized questionnaires for evaluating XR experiences.
You'll be able to compare the technical implementation and optimization strategies for VR deployment and contrast various implementation methods.

L45.lecture_goal: Apply empirical methods to design, conduct, and evaluate interactive system implementations.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define empirical studies and outline the initial stages of the empirical research process.
You'll be able to explain the role of empirical evaluation and outline the requirements and stages for conducting a usability study.
You'll be able to distinguish between testable and non-testable research questions and identify the variables used in experimental design.

L46.lecture_goal: design, execute, and statistically validate empirical studies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to differentiate between testable and untestable research questions, select representative participants, and identify critical considerations for designing a reliable empirical study.
You'll be able to compare within-subject and between-subjects experimental designs and analyze strategies to mitigate the practice effect.
You'll be able to explain the necessity of statistical significance and apply statistical tests to validate experimental results.

L47.lecture_goal: understand the complete process of designing, executing, and analyzing empirical studies for virtual reality system implementation.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the stages of system evaluation and describe the methodology, setup, and tools used to conduct a controlled VR experiment.
You'll be able to analyze quantitative results demonstrating how user presence and prior experience affect perception in virtual environments.
You'll be able to evaluate the impact of a VR system on user sickness and summarize the key steps of the empirical evaluation process.

L48.lecture_goal: Analyze the various methodologies used in system implementation, comparing traditional development cycles with modern Agile approaches.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the stages of system development, from requirement gathering and the design-prototype-evaluate cycle through implementation, testing, and usability evaluation.
You'll be able to compare traditional and Agile development methods, detailing the limitations of traditional approaches and the iterative process of Agile.
You'll be able to summarize key concepts in system implementation and identify future learning objectives.

L49.lecture_goal: Analyze the core principles, trade-offs, and frameworks required to optimize immersive VR experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to differentiate between optimization perspectives and define the goals and trade-offs of experience and resource optimization in XR.
You'll be able to identify and categorize the factors contributing to cyber sickness and define the trade-off between sickness mitigation and maintaining user presence.

You'll be able to compare user-controlled and system-controlled virtual tours, analyze the objectives of system-controlled tours, and explain how matching instantaneous walking speed improves realism.
You'll be able to summarize the VR optimization framework and the critical role of presence.

L50.lecture_goal: Develop a comprehensive understanding of how to model and optimize realistic movement within virtual reality environments.

objectives.text: You'll be able to outline the process of developing a realistic walking behavior model and describing the findings from the speed estimation study.
You'll be able to explain the difference between actual and perceived speed and model the relationship between movement and visual speed using visual gain.
You'll be able to evaluate the effectiveness of different walking speed models and summarize the limitations and future steps for VR optimization.

L51.lecture_goal: Develop a comprehensive understanding of how to optimize VR experiences and solve the associated pathfinding problems for efficient virtual tours.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the foundational concepts of optimizing VR experiences by controlling exposure duration and analyzing the methods and limitations of such control.
You'll be able to describe the characteristics of semi-interactive VR tours and define the specific optimization problems involved in creating an efficient tour.
You'll be able to formulate and solve the optimal POI travel problem by transforming it into a Traveling Salesman Problem and applying a two-phase algorithm.

L52.lecture_goal: Understand the principles and methods used to formulate and solve complex pathfinding problems for optimizing VR experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define the core problem of maximizing points of interest coverage within a time constraint.
You'll be able to formulate the path optimization problem by defining node importance and calculating total waiting time.
You'll be able to explain the relationship between the VR path optimization problem and VRP with Profit.
You'll be able to outline the algorithm and explain the refined optimal path formulation for VR experience optimization.

L53.lecture_goal: Master the techniques required to optimize VR navigation and exploration paths using graph theory and optimization algorithms.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare navigation optimization approaches and determine optimal paths for VR exploration based on time and experience constraints.
You'll be able to describe the methodology for converting a physical site into a weighted graph and apply optimization algorithms (TSP/VRPP) to find optimal paths.
You'll be able to summarize the key concepts of VR experience optimization and outline the focus of the next lecture.

L54.lecture_goal: understand the principles and processes involved in optimizing resource requirements for virtual reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define the challenges of VR resource optimization and justify the necessity of optimizing client-side hardware.
You'll be able to describe the fundamental principles of computer graphics, including the components and data flow of a generic graphics system.
You'll be able to explain the mechanisms of image rendering, the requirements for display refresh, and the structure of the 3D graphics pipeline.

L55.lecture_goal: Analyze the core components and representation challenges necessary for optimizing 3D rendering in VR systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the function and stages of the 3D graphics pipeline, including coordinate transformations.
You'll be able to identify the fundamental challenges in object representation and describe the major techniques used in VR systems.
You'll be able to summarize the stages of the 3D graphics pipeline and its implementation flexibility.

L56.lecture_goal: Understand the fundamental processes and mathematical models required for optimizing resource usage in VR rendering.

objectives.text: You'll be able to review computer graphics fundamentals and describe the stages of the 3D graphics pipeline.
You'll be able to apply transformations using matrices to position objects and explain how lighting models simulate color computation.
You'll be able to analyze and implement advanced lighting techniques, including intensity attenuation and mapping continuous values to device levels.

L57.lecture_goal: Understand the complete process of transforming 3D scene data into a viewable 2D image while considering VR resource constraints.

objectives.text: You'll be able to review the 3D graphics pipeline stages and understand the need for VR resource optimization.
You'll be able to explain how 3D scenes are projected onto 2D screens and describe the transformations that constitute the 3D viewing pipeline.

You'll be able to differentiate between projection types, explain the use of canonical view volumes, and describe the sequence of transformations for projection and viewport mapping using camera parameters.
You'll be able to explain the purpose and mechanism of clipping and hidden surface removal.

L58.lecture_goal: understand the complete architecture and computational demands of modern VR graphics systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the fundamental mechanics of 3D rendering, including the stages of the graphics pipeline, coordinate mapping, and efficient line drawing algorithms.
You'll be able to describe the computational challenges of VR rendering, such as aliasing, and how APIs and libraries simplify the implementation of graphics pipelines.
You'll be able to analyze the layered architecture of a VR system and the necessity and function of GPUs for parallel graphics processing.

L59.lecture_goal: master the principles and strategies required for efficient resource optimization in virtual reality environments.

objectives.text: You'll be able to apply theoretical knowledge to VR system design and analyze the computational challenges of rendering large, multimodal VR content.
You'll be able to explain how cloud computing and specific strategies optimize resource usage for both standalone and cloud-based VR/AR systems.
You'll be able to summarize resource optimization techniques and the relevance of computer graphics in VR deployment.

L60.lecture_goal: implement basic extended reality systems using the Unity platform.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how theoretical XR knowledge translates into practical system implementation and describe the Unity platform, its components, and its role in development.
You'll be able to identify the components of the Unity editor, define various extended reality systems, and explain the fundamental concepts of Game Objects, Components, and Prefabs.

L61.lecture_goal: build a comprehensive understanding of the technical and creative processes required to develop realistic 3D experiences in Unity.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how Unity constructs and renders a realistic 3D environment by utilizing different pipelines, object components, and native graphics APIs.
You'll be able to describe the core components and processes that enable realistic simulation, including physics, animation, and immersive audio.

L62.lecture_goal: master the process of developing complex, interactive applications by linking theoretical programming concepts to practical implementation methods in Unity.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how scripting allows customization beyond built-in Unity support and implement the process of creating and utilizing C# scripts within the Unity environment.
You'll be able to apply fundamental programming constructs, event functions, and object control mechanisms (coroutines, transforms) in Unity scripting.
You'll be able to explain how to handle user input and deploy a system using Unity's editor.
You'll be able to integrate external SDKs and apply these methods to build advanced applications, such as marker-based Augmented Reality.

L63.lecture_goal: Understand the course objectives and the scope of future learning in XR.

objectives.text: You'll be able to summarize the structure and content covered in the course modules.
You'll be able to define the course objective and identify relevant future learning areas in XR.
